title: Debating Remote Work Over Coffee
script: Wulan: [curious] Hendra, your company finally let everyone choose between office and home permanently, right? How's that actually working out?
Hendra: [thoughtful] Honestly, better than I expected, although it took a few months before I found a routine that actually functioned.
Wulan: [interested] What was difficult about it initially, given that working from home always sounded appealing to me?
Hendra: [honest] The main issue was boundaries. Without a commute separating work from home, my workday kept quietly stretching into the evening.
Wulan: [nodding] I've heard that from several people, even those who swore remote work would never affect their personal time.
Hendra: [continuing] Exactly. So I started closing my laptop physically, putting it in a drawer, instead of leaving it open on the table.
Wulan: [amused] That seems almost dramatic, closing a laptop in a drawer, but I suppose desperate situations need decisive solutions.
Hendra: [laughing] It sounds silly, yet it worked far better than any app or reminder I'd tried previously.
Wulan: [curious] What about focus, though? I assume home has more distractions than a proper office environment.
Hendra: [balanced] It depends. Fewer interruptions from colleagues, certainly, but more temptation to do laundry or scroll my phone.
Wulan: [thoughtful] So it's a trade-off rather than a clear improvement, despite everyone always talking about it so positively.
Hendra: [agreeing] Precisely. In spite of the flexibility, I do miss spontaneous conversations that solved problems faster than any scheduled call could.
Wulan: [considering] Would you ever go back to the office full time, given everything you've experienced so far?
Hendra: [reflective] Not entirely, no. I'd probably choose a hybrid arrangement, provided my team could still coordinate effectively across different days.
Wulan: [interested] That seems like the compromise most people I know eventually settle on, once the initial excitement fades.
Hendra: [nodding] It really does. Complete freedom sounds wonderful in theory, but structure, even loose structure, still matters enormously in practice.
Wulan: [smiling] Well, whatever you choose, it clearly beats my current commute, which somehow gets longer every single month.
Hendra: [sympathetic] That does sound miserable. Maybe it's time you asked your own manager about a hybrid option too.
